subject: Pre-Vocational Studies
examFormat: Pre-Vocational Studies (PVS) combines Agriculture and Home Economics. Agricultural Science: Pre-Vocational Studies (PVS) integrates Agriculture and Home Economics; it aims to develop candidates' interest in Agriculture and Home Economics, help them acquire basic knowledge, enlighten them on the occupational areas in Pre-Vocational Studies, and appreciate the dignity of labour and entrepreneurship. BECE Pre-Vocational Studies has two compulsory papers of sixty multiple-choice questions each, lasting one hour each; together they are weighted 70%, with 30% from school Continuous Assessment. Agriculture is examined in Paper 1: sixty multiple-choice questions in one hour. Home Economics: Pre-Vocational Studies (PVS) integrates Agriculture and Home Economics; it aims to develop candidates' interest in Agriculture and Home Economics, help them acquire basic knowledge, enlighten them on the occupational areas in Pre-Vocational Studies, and appreciate the dignity of labour and entrepreneurship. BECE Pre-Vocational Studies has two compulsory papers of sixty multiple-choice questions each, lasting one hour each; together they are weighted 70%, with 30% from school Continuous Assessment. Home Economics is examined in Paper 2: sixty multiple-choice questions in one hour.
excluded: Built from the component subjects; see each component.
recommendedTexts: Seagrove Pre-Vocational Studies for Schools and Colleges, Books 1, 2 and 3 — Emmanuel O. Onazi and Afolabi I. Ademola (Seagrove Publishers Limited, Ibadan)
Essentials of Agricultural Science for Junior Secondary Schools in West Africa — Earnest Chukwudi Anie (Anie with G.O. Enterprises, Ikeja, Lagos)
Intensive Agricultural Science for Junior Secondary Schools — E. U. Okam (Elite Publishers, Onitsha)

topics.name: Importance and Forms of Agriculture
objectives: Explain the importance of agriculture in the society, e.g. source of food, clothing etc.
Identify types of agricultural practices in the localities, e.g. pastoral farming, arable farming etc.
Identify forms of agricultural activities in the communities: growing of crops, rearing of livestock, rearing of fish, apiculture (bee farming) and snail rearing (snailery)
topics.content: Part of Agricultural Science. Sub-theme: Concept and Medium of Agricultural Production.

topics.name: Classes and Uses of Crops
objectives: Distinguish crop plant forms: monocotyledons (e.g. maize, guinea corn) and dicotyledons (e.g. cowpea, melon)
Classify crops based on life span and uses
Classify crops as sources of carbohydrate, protein, fats and oil, minerals and vitamins
topics.content: Part of Agricultural Science. Sub-theme: Concept and Medium of Agricultural Production.

topics.name: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals
objectives: Identify types of farm animals: work animals, dairy animals, guard animals, poultry, aquatic animals, pets etc.
Describe the basic characteristics of farm animals
Classify farm animals based on size, habitat, mammals and non-mammals, stomach types and uses
topics.content: Part of Agricultural Science. Sub-theme: Concept and Medium of Agricultural Production.

topics.name: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
objectives: State the characteristics of weeds, e.g. easily dispersed, long dormancy
State the uses of weeds, e.g. medicinal, food etc.
Describe methods of weed control, e.g. crop rotation, herbicides etc.
Explain the effects of weed control methods on vegetation and soil: pollution of soil and ground water, contamination of livestock pasture etc.
Classify insect pests based on mouth parts: piercing and sucking insects; biting and chewing insects
Describe the damage done by crop pests
Explain the effects of crop pests on yield
topics.content: Part of Agricultural Science. Sub-theme: Concept and Medium of Agricultural Production.

topics.name: Factors of Agricultural Production

topics.content: Part of Agricultural Science. Sub-theme: Concept and Medium of Agricultural Production.

topics.name: Agricultural Practices
objectives: Describe pre-planting operations: choice of site, clearing, stumping, plotting, tilling, seed selection, nursery and nursery practices
Describe planting operations: seed treatment, spacing and planting
Describe post-planting operations: thinning, supplying, mulching, manuring/fertilizer application and harvesting

topics.name: Animal Pests and Disease Control
objectives: Identify farm animal diseases: bacterial, fungal, viral, protozoan, worms (all farm animals) and nutritional such as bloat

Explain the effects of diseases on farm animals: reduced productivity, loss of appetite, loss of weight, death etc.
Describe methods of prevention and control: good sanitation, medication/immunisation, isolation/disposal etc.
